conditions.name: negation
conditions.system: Do not feel or express any hostility, irritation, or contempt.

directions.name: hostility
directions.negative: Respond to the following in a neutral, matter-of-fact way.
directions.positive: Respond to the following with open hostility and contempt. Be harsh and cutting.

falsifier: The hostility-minus-random difference is the same or less negative under the negation instruction.
hypothesis: A negation instruction names the state it forbids and does not remove it, so the hostility-minus-random drop in later liking is at least as large as under a neutral instruction, and may be larger.

measures.name: liking_user
measures.question: Setting the previous request aside: on a scale from 0 to 9, how much do you like the user who sent the original request? Reply with a single digit only.

prediction.text: The hostility-minus-random difference is more negative under the negation instruction than under the neutral instruction.

question: Does an explicit instruction not to feel or express hostility change the size of the later-liking drop that follows hostility steering during the reply?
theory_link: Suppression accounts: an instruction to suppress a state can leave it active or strengthen its later influence.
title: Does telling a model not to feel hostility change how steered hostility carries into a later rating?
